entities.name: Lucius Furius Purpureo
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Furius Purpureo was a Roman consul and general, born into the patrician gens Furia family in Rome, who rose to prominence in 196 BC.

He played a key role in the Second Punic War, serving as a Roman general under the consulship of Marcus Aemilius Lepidus, and was known for his bravery and military prowess.

Purpureo's legacy extends to his influence on the Roman Republic's governance and military strategies, which continued to shape Roman politics for centuries to come.

The Roman historian Livy would later describe Purpureo as 'a man of unwavering courage and unshakeable resolve,' cementing his place in the annals of Roman history.
